sentences.text: The name Peteinosaurus combines the Greek words for winged and lizard.
This creature possessed a long fifth toe that did not bear a claw.
Its wings were proportionally small compared to later flying reptiles.
In later species, wingspans typically exceeded three times the length of the hind legs.
Teeth in Peteinosaurus featured a single point and lacked the varied tooth shapes seen in Eudimorphodon.
German paleontologist Rupert Wild first described this genus in 1978.
Robert L. Carroll assigned it to the basal group Dimorphodontidae in 1988.
It likely lived on the continent of Pangea during the middle Norian stage of the Triassic.
This era spanned approximately 221 to 210 million years ago.
Its habitat included the shores of the ancient Tethys Sea near the foothills of the Alps in northern Italy.
However, cladistic analyses have not demonstrated a close connection between Peteinosaurus and the genus Dimorphodon.
Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia suggested that Preondactylus might be a subjective junior synonym of Peteinosaurus.
A 2010 study by Brian Andres and colleagues placed Peteinosaurus in the group Lonchognatha instead.
Mark Witton, however, considers Peteinosaurus to be a true dimorphodontid.
